To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

TUDCA is effective in preventing colchicine-induced cholestasis by preserving bile-salt transport, and that this action is related to the detergent effect of TUDCA on the organelle lipoprotein membranes and to the preservation of intracellular bile-salt transport.

UDCA, especially TUDCA, can exert anti-cholesteric action by maintaining bile flow even in the presence of microtubule dysfunction, and that this effect is associated with preservation of the integrity of intracellular transport and organelle membrane structure.

TUDCA, in contrast to TCA, can be secreted from the liver in colchicine- pretreated rats without microtubular function, and that the cytoprotection of UDCA may be due to the detergent action of its taurine conjugate inside the hepatocyte.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cytoprotectant effects of TUDC and the possible mechanisms involved in this effect.
the mechanism of action of UDCA in cholestatic disorders and suggests a possible new therapeutic approach to cholestatic liver diseases.
the mechanism by which UDCA and/or its conjugates exert anti-cholesteric effects and/or cytoprotective action in the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

UDCA and its taurine-conjuate are effective cytoprotective agents in the liver, and that the anti-cholestasis action of UDCA is mainly due to the preservation of the intrahepatocellular transport system.

UDCA, in its conjugated form, is able to protect the hepatocytes from colchicine-induced cholestasis, and that the protective effect is mediated by the bile-salt detergent effect and by the preservation of microtubules.
TUDCA may have a protective effect on the liver, and that the protective effects may be exerted by both the microtubule-independent and microtubule-dependent mechanisms.

TUDCA is a more potent choleretic and anti-cholestic agent than UDCA, and that the cytoprotection of UDCA is exerted by both microtubule-independent bile-salt transport and conjugation with tautine.
